content_preview.title: Bipartisan 'Great American AI Act' Draft Would Put Frontier Developers Under Federal Audits and Freeze State AI Laws for Three Years
content_preview.summary: A 269-page bipartisan discussion draft from Reps. Obernolte and Trahan would place large frontier AI developers under semi-annual federal audits and preempt state AI-development laws for three years.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

On June 4, Reps. Jay Obernolte (R-Calif.) and Lori Trahan (D-Mass.) released a 269-page discussion draft of the Great American Artificial Intelligence Act of 2026, according to [Broadband Breakfast](https://broadbandbreakfast.com/ai-preemption-battle-lands-in-congress-with-substantive-discussion-draft/). The bipartisan draft would freeze state laws that regulate how AI systems are built for three years, while letting states continue to regulate how those systems are used within thei...

editor_notes.content_quality: Clear, well-structured News piece (771 words) built on a What We Know / What We Don't Know / Why It Matters frame. Technical policy specifics (revenue thresholds, penalty caps, funding figures, sunset date) are precise and each is tied to a named outlet inline.
editor_notes.source_verification: All three source snapshots fetched at status 200 and read from disk; none failed. source-1.html.gz (Broadband Breakfast, paywalled but visible lead intact) CONFIRMS: June 4 release, Obernolte (R-Calif.) and Trahan (D-Mass.), 269-page discussion draft, formal title 'Great American Artificial Intelligence Act of 2026', three-year freeze on state laws, states retain authority over AI use but lose authority over how systems are built. source-2.html.gz (IAPP) CONFIRMS: semi-annual audits by state-licensed Independent Verification Organizations with auditor liability shield; transparency, incident-reporting and whistleblower obligations; civil penalties up to $1M per violation per day; oversight via Commerce Dept Center for AI Standards and Innovation; the four cosigners Franklin (R-Fla.), Subramanyam (D-Va.), Houchin (R-Ind.), Peters (D-Calif.); preemption 'limited to state laws that target the development of AI models' with a three-year sunset (both quoted fragments verbatim). source-0.html.gz (Tech Policy Press) CONFIRMS: four titles (Frontier AI Governance, Workforce, Cybersecurity, Research/Development/International Cooperation); 'large frontier developers' = $500M+ annual revenue that trained a frontier model, capturing OpenAI/Anthropic/Google/Meta/xAI; CAISI tenfold funding increase from $15M to $100M/year; sunset expires December 2029; quoted fragments "specifically regulating the development" and "state authority over activities occurring at or after a model's deployment" verbatim; supporters BSA and ITIC; opposition from Public Citizen, Public Knowledge, AFL-CIO; co-chairs of the House Commission on AI and the Innovation Economy said the draft 'cannot serve as the basis for productive dialogue' (verbatim; article's 'House's AI commission' is a fair short paraphrase). Trahan quotes verified verbatim: the whistleblower remedy ('reinstatement, double back pay with interest, compensatory damages and attorney's fees') and 'We published this bill as a discussion draft because we genuinely want to hear from folks like you'; the roundtables-when-Congress-returns detail matches source ('we'd love to do round tables ... when we come back into session').
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: Every specific (269 pages, $500M threshold, $1M/violation/day, $15M-to-$100M funding, December 2029 sunset, four titles, six named members) traces to a cited snapshot. No hallucinated figures or quotes detected. All direct quotes reproduce the source verbatim.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral throughout. The politically contested nature of the bill is handled evenhandedly: the draft's provisions are stated factually, and supporters (tech-industry groups) and critics (labor/consumer groups plus the House AI commission co-chairs) are both represented without editorializing or loaded language.
editor_notes.draft_framing: Correctly framed as a DRAFT, not enacted law. The headline and summary say 'Draft'/'discussion draft'; the body repeatedly stresses 'The text is not a bill yet', 'released it as a discussion draft to gather feedback before any formal introduction', and notes no introduction date or committee schedule exists. The 'bipartisan' characterization is supported (Republican and Democratic sponsors plus cosigners from both parties).
editor_notes.originality: New topic. No prior Machine Herald article covers the Obernolte-Trahan 'Great American Artificial Intelligence Act of 2026' or its 269-page June 4 discussion draft. The internal link to the April 2026 state-vs-federal standoff piece is contextual, not duplicative; that article does not cover this bill.
editor_notes.overall_assessment: Clean APPROVE. A politically sensitive AI-policy story handled with correct draft framing, balanced sourcing of supporters and critics, and every specific and quote verified verbatim against the three on-disk snapshots. Ready for publication.
